slides.say: A school has N students, and g of them are girls. Twenty-five percent of the girls play chess. What percent of all the students are girls who play chess?
There are letters in the question and in the choices. That's a hint that we can plug in numbers. We'll solve it in two different ways, by plugging in numbers, and then the math way.
Let's start by plugging in numbers. Like in psychometric thinking, check the restrictions first. Then choose easy allowed numbers. If choices give the same result, try another allowed example.
Let's use a hundred students, so each percent is one student. Let forty be girls. Forty is allowed and divides easily into quarters. So N is a hundred, and g is forty.
Twenty-five percent of the girls play chess. A quarter of forty is ten girls.
We compare those ten girls with all the students. Ten out of a hundred is ten percent. So our target is ten percent.

Now test the choices with these numbers. Choice number one says g over four N percent. Four times a hundred is four hundred. Forty over four hundred percent is a tenth of a percent, not ten percent. Out.

Choice number two says a hundred g over N percent. A hundred times forty is four thousand. Four thousand over a hundred is forty. That's forty percent of the students, all the girls, not just the girls who play chess. Out.
at: not just the girls who play chess

slides.say: Choice number three says twenty-five g over N percent. Twenty-five times forty is a thousand. A thousand over a hundred is ten. So this choice gives ten percent, our target.
at: Twenty-five times forty is a thousand
A thousand over a hundred is ten

slides.say: Choice number three matches, but we must check choice number four too. A match doesn't rule out an untested choice. Choice number four says twenty-five N over g percent. Twenty-five times a hundred is two thousand five hundred. Dividing by forty cannot give ten. Ten times forty is only four hundred. So this is not ten percent. Out.
at: So this is not ten percent

slides.say: Only choice number three gives ten percent. If two choices had given ten percent, we'd pick new numbers and test only those two. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the math way, with the letters. We start again from the givens. Twenty-five percent of the girls is a quarter of g, so g over four girls play chess.
To get a percent, we take the part over the whole, times a hundred. The part is g over four, and the whole is all the students, N.
at: we take the part over the whole

slides.say: g over four, divided by N, is g over four N.
Times a hundred, it's a hundred g over four N. A hundred over four is twenty-five, so it's twenty-five g over N.
at: A hundred over four is twenty-five

slides.say: g over four N is the fraction of the students. To write it as a percent, we multiply that number by a hundred first. Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
